blueprint_topic: Management of Care — home-health referral, payer eligibility, documentation, and continuity of skilled care
stem: A Medicare beneficiary is preparing for discharge after orthopedic surgery. The client needs a walker and another person's help to leave home, leaving home requires considerable effort, and intermittent skilled physical therapy is needed. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Coordinate a home-health referral and have the discharge team verify the required homebound, skilled-service, certification, and plan-of-care documentation.
options.B: Treat walker use and the need for skilled physical therapy as sufficient Medicare eligibility and proceed without verifying the remaining coverage requirements.
options.C: Delay the referral because occasional trips for medical care exclude the client from Medicare homebound status despite the effort required to leave home.
options.D: Plan outpatient physical therapy instead because Medicare home health does not use skilled physical therapy as a qualifying service after surgery.

rationale: A is correct. Current CMS guidance states that Medicare home-health eligibility requires the patient to be confined to the home, be under the care of a physician or allowed practitioner, receive services under an established and periodically reviewed plan of care, and need a qualifying skilled service such as physical therapy. CMS also requires certification and supporting documentation of homebound status and skilled-service need. The stem supplies facts consistent with the homebound criteria but does not authorize the nurse to assume that all Medicare requirements are complete, so the nurse should coordinate the referral and ensure the discharge process verifies the required documentation. B is incorrect because walker use plus skilled PT need does not by itself establish every Medicare requirement. C is incorrect because CMS permits short or infrequent absences, including for health care, without automatically defeating homebound status. D is incorrect because physical therapy is expressly listed as a qualifying skilled service for the Medicare home-health benefit when the other requirements are met.
educational_objective: Coordinate Medicare home-health referral by recognizing the homebound and skilled-service criteria while ensuring certification, plan-of-care, and supporting documentation requirements are verified rather than assuming eligibility from mobility limitation alone.

source_locator: CMS 'Home Health Services' lines 746-779: Medicare home-health coverage requires certification; qualifying patients must be confined to home, under physician/allowed-practitioner care, receive services under a periodically reviewed plan of care, and need qualifying skilled care including physical therapy; certification includes homebound status, skilled-service need, plan of care and face-to-face requirements. CMS lines 786-804: homebound Criterion 1 includes walker/supportive-device use or another person's help; Criterion 2 requires normally unable to leave home and considerable/taxing effort; short or infrequent absences for health care and specified other reasons do not automatically defeat homebound status. CMS lines 816-818: supporting records must justify skilled-service need and homebound status. Medicare.gov lines 54-59 independently confirms part-time/intermittent skilled-service need plus homebound criteria. correction_summary: Original Q1873 had a 237-character correct answer, obvious absolute-word distractors and an answer-length cue. All four options were rebuilt into realistic Medicare discharge-planning alternatives of comparable length. The correct answer now requires distinguishing likely homebound/skilled-service facts from the additional certification, plan-of-care and documentation requirements that must still be verified.

option_audit.A: Correct; coordinates the referral while preserving the distinction between clinical facts suggesting eligibility and the full CMS certification/documentation requirements.
option_audit.B: Plausible shortcut; incorrect because walker use and skilled PT need do not establish every Medicare home-health requirement.
option_audit.C: Plausible homebound-definition misconception; incorrect because limited medical or other infrequent absences can coexist with homebound status.
option_audit.D: Plausible service-coverage misconception; incorrect because skilled physical therapy is expressly a qualifying home-health service when other criteria are met.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option depends on all/only/never/solely/always/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 156, B 160, C 153, D 146 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and the choices are tightly balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four choices are action-oriented Medicare discharge/referral decisions and remain clinically plausible at first read.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified in the pre-stage audit. B omits required eligibility elements, C misstates permitted absences, and D misstates PT coverage. Post-fetch adversarial reread remains required.
